store_data.about_the_game:
SAVE US, DOCTOR FAUST! 

Become a medieval doctor in a city ravaged by disease, war, and desperation.

In Save Us, Doctor Faust!, there are no quest markers telling you what to do, no glowing ingredients, and no magic button that instantly solves every medical problem.

You must learn, observe, experiment, and make your own decisions.

Study diseases in your medical textbook. Examine your patients. Prepare medicines by hand. Manage scarce resources. And remember: a mistake in the laboratory can cost someone their life.

LEARN MEDICINE. YOURSELF.

Your medical textbook is your most important tool.

Study diseases, symptoms, treatments, and medicinal ingredients. Take notes directly on its pages with a pencil. Write down your discoveries, useful combinations, symptoms, and anything else you think might help you survive as a doctor.

But the game will not hold your hand.

There are no automatic diagnoses. No objective markers telling you which medicine to create. No convenient list of ingredients that magically solves every problem.

If you want to become a better doctor, you have to study.

Read. Observe. Remember.

Your knowledge is your greatest tool.

PREPARE MEDICINE BY HAND

Medicine is not created by simply clicking a recipe.

Raw ingredients must be carefully processed before they can become useful.

Grind herbs, minerals, and other substances in a mortar and pestle. Prepare your ingredients and turn them into the components needed for more complex remedies.

The way you process your ingredients matters.

A careless doctor can waste precious resources — or create something that harms the patient instead of helping them.

DISTILL. EXTRACT. TRANSFORM.

Some ingredients cannot simply be mixed together.

Use a still to distill alcohol, create liquid substrates, and prepare emulsions. Carefully transform raw materials into new medicinal components.

The process of creating a medicine is just as important as the ingredients themselves.

Experiment with different methods, discover new possibilities, and learn how different substances can be combined.

MIX WITH PRECISION

Some combinations require more than simply pouring ingredients into the same container.

Use a centrifuge to mix and enhance your compounds. Turn the handle yourself and control the process as you prepare your medicine.

Every remedy is the result of knowledge, preparation, and careful experimentation.

And if you get it wrong...

Your patient may pay the price.

DIAGNOSE YOUR PATIENTS

Every patient is different.

Start by asking questions. Listen carefully to their complaints and symptoms. Their answers may reveal important clues — or mislead you.

Then examine their body.

Look for visible signs of disease. Compare what you see with what you have learned. Combine the information from the interview and the examination to determine what is truly wrong.

There is no magic diagnosis button.

You are the doctor.

EVERY LIFE HAS A PRICE

The city is under siege.

Disease is spreading. Resources are limited. Medicine is expensive. And there are more people who need help than you can possibly save.

You will have to decide how to spend your money and ingredients.

Treat a sick child who cannot afford the medicine?

Or save a wealthy nobleman who can pay enough to keep your clinic running?

What if the nobleman is cruel? What if the child's treatment requires ingredients that could save several other patients?

There are no easy answers.

Every decision has a cost.

A CITY THAT REMEMBERS YOUR CHOICES

Your actions will shape the fate of the city.

The war raging beyond its walls may seem distant, but your work as a doctor can influence what happens outside your clinic.

Treat the right people. Make the right choices. Keep the city alive.

Your actions can change the balance of power and even alter the course of the war.

MANAGE WHAT YOU HAVE

Money and ingredients are limited.

Buy what you need. Plan ahead. Decide which medicines are worth preparing and which resources you can afford to spend.

Grow some of your own medicinal plants and cultivate valuable ingredients yourself.

But you will never have enough for everyone.

Who will you save?

NO TWO DOCTORS WILL PLAY THE SAME WAY

Will you become a careful scholar who studies every disease before treating a patient?

A resourceful alchemist who experiments with strange combinations?

A ruthless businessman who treats those who can pay?

Or a doctor who tries to save everyone — no matter the cost?

The city is in your hands.

Study. Diagnose. Experiment. Decide.

SAVE US, DOCTOR FAUST!

store_data.about_the_game:
One accidental message can change everything.

You find your way into the private channel of Elizabeth, a mysterious cyberpunk model who hides her true feelings behind neon lights, explicit photos, and a confident smile.

At first, you are nothing more than a stranger in her private messages. But with every new conversation, the distance between you begins to disappear.

Over the course of ten days, you will chat with Elizabeth, assist her during private streams, participate in unusual experiments, uncover her secrets, and gradually earn the trust of a woman who has grown used to seeing everyone around her as either a viewer or a customer.

Your selected replies appear as real outgoing messages. You can be shy, playful, flirtatious, honest, or cautious enough to stop at the right moment. Elizabeth pays attention not only to what you say, but also to how carefully you treat her desires, emotions, and personal boundaries.

Can you become more than just another subscriber?

And what will happen when your virtual connection finally moves beyond the screen?

Game Features

— Ten story-rich days following the gradual development of your relationship, from an accidental conversation to your first real-life meeting.

— An immersive messenger interface featuring incoming messages, multi-part replies, photos, typing indicators, and a scrollable chat history.

— 143 explicit illustrations unlocked throughout the story and collected in a dedicated gallery.

— Plenty of dialogue choices. Be shy, romantic, bold, observant, playful, or careful.

— Gradual erotic progression through private photos, exclusive streams, video calls, remote experiments, and fully explicit intimate scenes.

— Interactive mini-games woven into the story, including QuickTap, signal tests, remote access challenges, security investigations, and other mechanics.

— Trust and personal boundaries matter. Your decisions affect the tone of conversations, Elizabeth’s reactions, and the development of your relationship.

— A neon cyberpunk atmosphere filled with private channels, digital interfaces, restricted systems, and secrets hidden behind Elizabeth’s public persona.

She is used to people wanting access to her body.

Perhaps, for the first time, someone will want to know the real woman behind the neon signal.

All characters involved in explicit scenes are adults. Every intimate encounter is consensual and based on mutual agreement.

store_data.about_the_game:
Want an Engineer who can revive pieces back? Or a Rook that can move 1 square diagonally? Maybe a Pawn that can also go backwards?

Well you got all of that in Chaos Chess.

Chaos Chess is still chess. Same board. Same checkmate. Same feeling that you should have seen that coming three moves ago. 

What changes is the army. You get a point budget, a piece limit, and a pile of blueprints — classic pieces, fairy movers, siege junk, kings that do more than sit in the corner. You build a loadout, take it into a match, and find out whether the theory holds up.

No loot ladders. No pay-to-win pieces. Tokens you earn in play unlock the roster and a few board skins. The rest is sitting with the board until something clicks.

Army Lab

Drag owned pieces onto the board. Watch the budget. Save the ones that feel right.

Every piece shows its move diagram, the actual rules in plain language, and a short scrap of lore if you care about that kind of thing. Some revive allies. Some explode on contact. Some just sit there and make three squares in front of them miserable for the enemy. You will put two pieces together that look brilliant and lose to a pawn that learned to step backward.

The roster

Start with the familiar set if you want. Or don't.

Open Chaos Packs with tokens you earn from matches. Commons stack up. Rares and better show up often enough that the collection doesn't feel like a second job. Pity on every pack: at least one Rare or better. Stack caps keep things from getting silly.

War Machines. Sappers. Hot Cauldrons. Engineers who treat the dead like reusable timber. If it has a legal move pattern and fits the budget, it can end up on your back row.

Match

  • Play against AI across a range of difficulties, including ones that will make you doubt your life choices.

  • Local hotseat when someone is sitting next to you.

  • Quick Random if you want a loadout and a fight without opening the Lab first.

  • Play Online by launching the online version. Quick matchmaking or invite code style.

Click a piece, read what it actually does, then move. Illegal attempts get told off. The board does not care about your plan.

Puzzles

Mate in one, two, or three. Built-in challenges to learn the odd pieces without burning a whole match.

There is also a Puzzle Designer: place pieces, set the mate depth, playtest until it is honest, then save it. Publish to the Workshop when you are ready to hand your trap to strangers.

Skin Lab

Board skins and piece presentation, unlocked with the same tokens. Preview before you commit. Classic wood, neon circuit, rune stone — or stick with the original and get back to the game.

If that sounds like you

Chaos Chess is for people who like chess enough to argue about it, and variants enough to open a spreadsheet. Build an army. Break a few habits. Lose to Nightmare. Open one more pack. Try again.

Build the Card Shop You’ve Always Wanted

Start with a humble local shop and grow it into the ultimate destination for trading card fans. Stock sought-after booster packs, keep your shelves full, and give every customer a reason to come back.

Create a Store With Your Own Style

Make the shop truly yours. Freely arrange displays, furniture, decor, and play areas to create a one-of-a-kind space for collecting, shopping, and friendly competition.

Hire and Train Your Team

A successful store takes more than one person. Hire dependable staff and develop their skills to help restock products, assist customers, and handle daily operations as your business grows.

More Than a Shop Owner—Become a Champion

When the workday ends, it is your turn to play. Build your own deck, refine your strategy, and improve through tactical card battles. Rise from city-level events to the World Championship and fight for the highest honor.

store_data.about_the_game:
Merge Co.

Build the ultimate toy collection!

Merge Co. is a cozy and satisfying merge game where you combine adorable toys to unlock bigger, rarer, and more valuable collectibles. Merge matching toys, discover exciting new creations, and fill your toy box with unique treasures!

Every merge brings a new surprise. With simple mechanics and relaxing gameplay, Merge Co. is perfect whether you're playing for a few minutes or settling in for a long, cozy session.

Features

🧸 Discover hundreds of adorable toys.

✨ Merge identical toys to create new and more valuable ones.

🎁 Unlock rare and special collectibles.

🌈 Enjoy a colorful, cozy, and relaxing atmosphere.

🏆 Complete your collection and discover every toy.

🎮 Easy to learn, satisfying to master.

Every Merge is a New Discovery!

Start with simple toys and work your way up to colorful trains, cute robots, rockets, cars, and many more delightful collectibles. Plan your merges, manage your space wisely, and build the ultimate toy collection.

With charming visuals, relaxing music, and satisfying merge effects, Merge Co. delivers a cozy experience that's fun for players of all ages.

Merge. Discover. Collect.

store_data.about_the_game:
Descend into the Swamp

Every step draws you deeper into a place that refuses to let you go. Explore an endless procedurally generated swamp where reality slowly begins to unravel.

Explore an Endless Swamp

Every journey is different. Traverse procedurally generated boardwalks, discover forgotten paths, and venture deeper into an ever-changing marshland where no two expeditions are the same.

Uncover Forgotten Fragments

Discover mysterious objects, forgotten memories, and remnants left behind by those who came before you. Piece together the hidden history of the swamp through exploration rather than exposition.

Hold on to Your Sanity

The deeper you descend, the less you can trust your own senses. Preserve your sanity as reality twists around you and familiar paths begin to change.

Atmospheric Psychological Horror

Backswamps focuses on atmosphere, exploration, environmental storytelling, and psychological horror rather than combat. Every sound, every shadow, and every step contributes to an unsettling journey into the unknown.

Every Expedition is Unique

Procedurally generated environments ensure that each descent offers new paths, new discoveries, and new dangers waiting beneath the fog.

Something Watches

The swamp is not empty.

store_data.about_the_game:
Uncover the secrets of Lumeria

The kingdom of Lumeria is in it's twilight years. Light hasn't touched the land in ages and no one knows what must be done to restore it. Whispers travel through the kingdom about a source of infinite light. A power so great that it could be the very answer to the kingdoms problem. 

Make new friends or enemies

Battle through the abandoned corridors of Lumeria and face the nightmares that haunt the citizens of this once great kingdom. Forge alliances and choose whether to help the lamps you find on your journey. Unlock the secrets of this world and make meaningful choices that will affect the lives of those you meet as well as yours. The fate of the kingdom is in your hands, will you ascend to become its saviour?

Character Customization

Upgrade your character through meaningful stat progression by choosing which specific stat you want strengthened and utilize weapons that compliment the playstyle you have chosen. Break the game, there is no cap to how strong you can become, push the game to it's limits. Equip trinkets found around Lumeria and cast devastating spells and abilities to gain an advantage over your foes. 

Strategic yet relaxed gameplay

Relaxed gameplay: The classic turn-based combat allows you to pick up and put down the game whenever you feel like it. No pausing required. Carefully choose when to attack, defend or use an item in order to survive the onslaught of enemies. Prepare your items and rush headfirst into the action.

store_data.about_the_game:
The kingdom has fallen. Magic is fading. Darkness is rising.

Step into the world of Realms of Wands, a dark fantasy action RPG where ancient kingdoms lie in ruins, powerful relics have been scattered across the land, and monstrous creatures roam forgotten realms. Every journey leads deeper into a world filled with danger, mystery, and legendary rewards.

Battle your way through cursed forests, abandoned castles, haunted crypts, frozen wastelands, volcanic caverns, and forgotten temples as you uncover the truth behind the collapse of the realm.

Master powerful weapons, unlock devastating spells, collect rare equipment, and create unique character builds to survive increasingly difficult enemies and colossal boss encounters.

Whether you're hunting for legendary loot, completing quests, or perfecting your build, every adventure offers new challenges and discoveries.

Features

  • Explore a handcrafted dark fantasy world filled with secrets.

  • Fast-paced real-time combat against monsters, undead, demons, and powerful bosses.

  • Discover and equip unique weapons, armour, relics, and magical artifacts.

  • Learn powerful spells and combine abilities to create your own combat style.

  • Complete quests and uncover the history of the fallen kingdoms.

  • Earn experience, level up, and unlock permanent character upgrades.

  • Craft stronger equipment and improve your arsenal.

  • Face epic boss battles that test your skill and strategy.

  • Discover hidden areas, rare treasures, and legendary loot.

  • Steam Achievements and Steam Cloud support.

  • Designed for keyboard and mouse, with future controller support planned.

Will You Restore the Realm?

The darkness continues to spread across the land, and only those brave enough to face impossible odds can stand against it.

Gather your weapons.

Master the arcane.

Challenge ancient evils.

Forge your legend.

The fate of the realm now rests in your hands.

store_data.about_the_game:
Stop the Curse, Save the town!

As the Witch's last Apprentice, you are given the task of ending the Curse your Master placed on the town. With 100 days left before the Curse is permanent, you must gather information about the ritual and find the needed ingredients to power a ritual to end the Curse.

Explore a Mysterious Town

The knowledge you need is in the town somewhere, hidden in half-remembered stories, favors, and locations. Explore the town, gather rumors, and supplies to break the curse. With over 15 locations and 20 NPCs with 2000+ story events, a large town awaits your exploration.

Get to know the various townsfolk

Everyone knows something to help and some have hidden secrets that you will need to uncover. Build relationships with townsfolk to get them to help you or try to go it alone and stop the curse on your own. Give gifts, complete requests, and find lost property to build up your relations with them, but beware more than one is hiding dark secrets that you will have to contend with!

Identify the Correct Ingredients

You need five ingredients to stop the curse, but ten exist. Quickly narrow down which ingredients you need using rumors and leads or risk running out of time to gather them all!

Manage Cutting back Thorns and Earning Money

The thorns are growing quickly and will need to be cut back. You must balance rituals, aid from townsfolk and your own efforts to keep them in check or risk the town being overrun by thorns before 100 days have passed.

Multiple Endings

Be good and honest or manipulative and sneaky, your actions and decisions will shape the ending of your story.  Compromise your morals for quick success or find legal and ethical ways to get access.

Multiple Achievements and Random Ingredients

With over 75 achievements and 3 difficulty levels, challenge yourself to play the game in unique and clever ways with the unique randomization of needed ingredients and events. Each run is unique and means several runs will be needed to see most of the content!

Hidden locations and NPCs

Of course, a town of secrets has hidden places to explore and NPCs to find. Discover the truth of the sewers and other mysteries!

store_data.about_the_game:
BOOT THE CARTRIDGE. CHOOSE YOUR PARTNER. DO NOT EJECT.

Do Not Eject is a retro handheld-inspired bullet heaven roguelite where corrupted game cartridges have trapped living digital creatures inside.

Choose your partner, insert a cartridge, and fight through waves of corrupted programs as your attacks evolve from a handful of projectiles into ridiculous combinations of ricochets, orbiting weapons, explosions, piercing shots, and chain reactions.

Defeat the corrupted guardian waiting at the end of each cartridge, restore it to the console, and unlock it as your next playable partner.

BUILD SOMETHING ABSURD

Every run starts small.

As you survive, you’ll install powerful Modules that fundamentally change how your attacks behave, stack Patches that strengthen your build, and equip Auxiliary Chips that add entirely new elemental interactions before the run even begins.

No two runs need to play the same.

A simple projectile can evolve into a screen-filling storm of bouncing, piercing, homing, exploding, and orbiting attacks. Automatic stat growth keeps the pacing fast, letting you focus on movement, positioning, and choosing the upgrades that create your next broken build.

RESCUE YOUR DIGITAL PARTNERS

Every cartridge hides a corrupted creature waiting to be restored.

Defeat its guardian to purify the cartridge and add that partner permanently to your collection.

Each playable partner features:

  • A unique weapon and combat style

  • A defining passive ability

  • Exclusive Modules

  • A permanent Memory Tree

  • New interactions with every Auxiliary Chip

The planned full game features ten elemental cartridges, each introducing a new partner, enemy roster, boss, and set of build possibilities.

EVERY RUN MOVES YOU FORWARD

Even failed runs matter.

Collect Data Bits, Core Shards, and Creature Mastery during every attempt, then return to upgrade your console, unlock new Auxiliary Chips, and permanently strengthen your favorite partners through their Memory Trees.

Failure isn’t a reset.

It’s another step toward rebuilding the console.

THE CORRUPTION NEVER STOPS GROWING

Restoring a cartridge is only the beginning.

Increase its Corruption Level to face faster enemies, tougher bosses, and increasingly dangerous encounters that push every build to its limit.

How much corruption can your favorite partner survive?

A CONSOLE WORTH SAVING

The console itself is your home.

Manage restored partners inside the Habitat, browse your discoveries in the Archive, improve your hardware through the Kernel Terminal, and slowly bring the abandoned system back to life one repaired cartridge at a time.

KEY FEATURES

  • Fast 8-10 minute bullet heaven runs with automatic combat

  • Build-breaking Modules that dramatically transform projectile behavior

  • Stackable Patches and elemental Auxiliary Chips for huge build variety

  • Unlockable digital partner creatures with unique weapons, passives, and progression

  • Permanent Creature Mastery and console-wide upgrades

  • Corruption Levels that expand replayability long after your first victory

  • Bosses that become playable partners after purification

  • A retro handheld-inspired console that serves as both hub world and progression system

  • Full keyboard, mouse, and controller support

Do Not Eject is currently in active development. Screenshots and footage currently feature the Data Cartridge, the first completed cartridge world. Additional cartridges, partner creatures, and elemental systems are planned for the full release.

store_data.about_the_game:
Clock out on time. Break the entire company on the way.

Tasks, reports, HR, and punch clocks have flooded the office. Three dogs who refuse to work overtime are fighting back with the only weapons they can find: office supplies. Doggo on Strike is a cute, darkly comic top-down survivor-like built for fast, ridiculous runs. You only control movement; every weapon attacks automatically. Level-ups pause the action and offer three choices, turning ordinary stationery into absurd crowd-clearing builds.

Three Dogs, Three Ways to Break the Rules

  • Intern Shiba: levels quickly and reaches a working build sooner.
  • Hoodie Slacker: exploits policy loopholes, rhythm, and sustain.
  • Hotheaded Vanguard: fights closer to danger for savage counters and burst damage.
Each dog changes the core rules of a run instead of acting as a simple skin.

24 Office Weapons. Fuse Them. Evolve Them.

  • Staplers, coffee, keyboards, resignation letters, and 20 more base skills use distinct trajectories, timing, range, and penetration.
  • 14 compatible pairs merge into entirely new fusion attacks.
  • 8 weapon-and-passive recipes evolve through elite chests.
  • Choose two charged ultimates from a roster of six and fire them when the workload becomes unbearable.

Six Workplace Battlegrounds, 8–10 Minutes Each

Fight from the Night Office and HR Interview Cubicles through the Printer Storm Line and all the way to the Cat Boss Final Review. Every stage has its own absurd office mechanic, scaling elites, and two bosses—twelve in total. The final boss must fall before Doggo can clock out.

More Than One Good Escape

Reveal enemies in the codex, uncover secrets hidden across all six stages, chase 42 playful achievements, and chain in-run Slack Orders that can change your build on the spot. No fire button. No homework-sized tutorial. Move, choose, grow stronger, and tear through the company.

store_data.about_the_game:
The oldest duel in space, replayed like day one - only better.

In 1962, on a PDP-1 computer the size of a wardrobe, a handful of MIT students invented one of the very first video games in history: Spacewar!. Two ships, a merciless star, and gravity as the only law.

This version doesn't go all the way back to the PDP-1: it's an adaptation of the 1980s MS-DOS version, the one that lit up the phosphor screens of a whole generation of PC players. We kept its soul - the vector lines, the unforgiving inertia, the twitchy duel - and opened it up to four players, online and on the couch alike.

A duel of precision and nerve


No lives, no XP bar: just you, your thrust, and an energy reserve that drains four times faster than it recharges. Every maneuver costs you.

  • Torpedo - fired along your velocity vector: inertia decides everything.
  • Phaser - a mid-range hitscan beam that tears through... and vaporizes incoming torpedoes.
  • Cloak - vanish from the radar, at a steep price.
  • Hyperspace - flee the impact... or reappear in the worst possible spot.
  • The planet - dead center: its gravity pulls you in, its touch disintegrates you.

Up to 4, anywhere


  • 1 to 4 players, local AND online, in the same game.
  • Bots with three temperaments - defensive, offensive, balanced: real opponents, not targets.
  • Two players on one keyboard, on a controller, or a mix of both.
  • Steam Deck compatible.

Built for game night


Planet or not, gravity or not, score limit: set up the match that suits you. Eleven languages, fully playable on keyboard or controller.

The duel that invented the genre. Now it's your turn to replay it.

store_data.about_the_game:
About this game

"Genesis: From Water to Stars" is a strategy exploration automation game with card synthesis gameplay.

Game Introduction

This is a game that combines card synthesis, resource management and automation on a single lively canvas.

Since it is a card game, here everything is a card. Yes, every card.

But they are more than just cards. People walk, trees shed leaves, fire smokes; the world you create with your own hands is alive, and at the same time, the cards you create will experience day and night and unexpected events.

So

It is also a synthesis game, which means the interactions and operations you need also have a feel of synthesis, even in the menu interface.

Who is this game for?

Players who like automation games

Players who enjoy exploration games

Players who enjoy card synthesis games

Players who like to explore step by step

Players who want to experience human history firsthand

Core Features

Start with simple natural elements and gradually discover food, tools, buildings, energy and technology. Recipes may require two, three or more materials, and some products can become the starting point for another long chain.

There is no fully prepared world waiting for you. Technology, shops, facilities, even the rules of day and night must be created by you. What you combine is not just a new card, but potentially a brand new way the world works.

The game doesn’t put all the answers in front of you. Quests give direction, experiments leave discoveries, inspiration points the way, and research reveals new cards. Each new recipe expands your world.

From natural origins to agriculture, industry and further technology, six chapters continuously push the same canvas into new eras. The journey begins with a few simple origins and ends among the stars.

The ultimate goal of the game is the "Stars and Sea". Yes, humanity once aimed for this, and this game will accompany you through the history of human development.

Finally, see what kind of world you can create.

store_data.about_the_game:
Build Complete Production Chains

Control the entire journey of a product—from raw material to store shelf.

Establish farms, mines, logging camps, factories, warehouses, and shops. Supply each facility with the resources it needs, balance production capacity across multiple stages, and create efficient logistics networks capable of serving entire regions.

Turn wheat into flour and bread, iron ore into steel and machinery, cotton into fabric and clothing, or crude oil into fuel and advanced industrial products. Expand simple workshops into interconnected industries as the world becomes more technologically developed.

A shortage at one stage can disrupt the entire chain, while excess production may fill warehouses and drive prices down. Successful growth requires more than building factories: every part of the system must work together.

Produce the Goods That Defined an Era

Manufacture products inspired by the real industrial history of the early and mid-20th century—from canned food, corn flakes, bottled milk, clothing, and household goods to typewriters, radios, appliances, steam-powered vehicles, and classic automobiles.

Watch familiar products emerge as technologies transform industry and everyday life. Follow their evolution through new materials, manufacturing methods, and technological generations.

Every product includes a historical note explaining its origins, development, production, and influence on society. Discover the stories behind familiar goods, learn about forgotten inventions, and see how once-revolutionary products became ordinary parts of everyday life.

The game uses historically recognizable product categories and original fictional brands, allowing you to create your own industrial history without simply repeating the real one.

Compete in a Living Economy

Markets respond dynamically to supply and demand.

Flooding a region with one product may reduce its price and profitability, while shortages can create valuable opportunities. Population, income, access to goods, regional resources, production costs, and the actions of competing companies all influence demand.

Set prices, control costs, secure access to valuable resources, and decide when to increase production or enter a different industry. Compete for customers, suppliers, market share, and the most promising regions.

A profitable product will not remain uncontested forever. Rival companies can expand into your markets, introduce alternatives, and research technologies of their own. Adapt to changing conditions—or watch a once-dominant industry fall behind.

Shape the Growth of Cities

Cities are active participants in the economy, not static decorations.

They need jobs, raw materials, consumer goods, and functioning industries to develop. A new factory can attract workers and support local businesses. Reliable access to products can improve living conditions and encourage further population growth. In turn, larger cities create new demand and provide a greater workforce.

Your decisions can transform a small settlement into a thriving industrial center. Poor planning, unemployment, shortages, or an overreliance on a single industry may slow its development.

Choose where to establish production centers, which cities to supply, and how each region should specialize. As your company grows, the world grows with it.

Shape Technological Progress

Research does more than unlock upgrades—it determines which technologies and products can exist in the world.

Develop new production methods, materials, engines, machines, and consumer goods. Become the first company to make a breakthrough, establish an entirely new industry, and gain a powerful advantage before competitors catch up.

Depending on the selected difficulty and game rules, technological progress may not be guaranteed. On more accessible settings, inventions can gradually enter the world on their own. Under more demanding rules, companies must discover them through research.

If nobody develops the internal combustion engine, gasoline-powered automobiles may never appear—and the world could continue relying on steam-powered transport. Familiar products might arrive decades later than they did in reality, emerge in a different form, or never be invented at all.

Every campaign can create its own alternative history of industrial progress.

Build Recognizable Brands

A product is more than the materials used to make it.

Create your own brands, improve product quality, and increase public awareness. Introduce distinctive product variants that stand apart from competing offers and turn ordinary goods into names recognized across the world.

A strong reputation can increase demand, inspire customer loyalty, and help your company defend its position even when competitors offer lower prices. Become known for affordable essentials, premium goods, technological innovation, or unique products that no other company can manufacture.

Build a brand that survives changing markets—and make your products symbols of their era.

Explore Vast Generated Worlds

Expand across vast procedurally generated maps with different geography, resources, cities, and economic opportunities in every campaign.

Some regions may provide abundant farmland but lack valuable minerals. Others can become industrial centers due to rich deposits, access to transport, or proximity to growing cities. Establish specialized regional economies and connect them through an increasingly complex production and distribution network.

Different starting conditions, difficulty levels, competitors, resources, markets, and paths of technological development make every world unique.

Key Features

  • Vast procedurally generated maps

  • Resource extraction, manufacturing, logistics, and retail

  • Complex multi-stage production chains

  • Historically inspired goods from the early and mid-20th century

  • Historical notes for every product

  • Dynamic prices driven by supply and demand

  • Competing companies and battles for market share

  • Cities that grow through jobs, industry, and access to goods

  • Research that shapes the technological progress of the entire world

  • Alternative industrial histories created by players and competitors

  • Product quality, unique goods, and brand recognition

  • Warehouses, inventories, production capacity, and regional distribution

  • Multiple difficulty levels and customizable game rules

  • Different markets, resources, and development paths in every campaign

Build industries. Create markets. Develop cities. Shape the future.

store_data.about_the_game:
DECEMBER 1980

It's the day after Christmas, and your dad is already back to work. The building will be mostly empty over the holidays, so he takes you along! But watching him work on spreadsheets isn't as exciting as you thought--so you decide to explore the building.

EXPLORE THE RESEARCH FACILITY

Graham Labs is one of the most prestigious computer research facilities in the country. Find what mysteries await behind locked doors, down dark ventilation shafts, and go deeper into the building than you should. Something's waiting in the basement for you, though. And it's been alone for a very long time.

FEATURES

  • Graphics: Retro PSX-style graphics.

  • Controls: Full support for keyboard/mouse and controllers.

  • Playtime: Red Father can be played in 2-3 hours.

PLATFORMS

  • Windows 10/11

  • Linux & SteamOS

  • Steam Deck

store_data.about_the_game:
Nothing ends. It only casts a longer shadow.

Earth is dying.

Water is rationed. Fuel has become scarce. Electricity fails without warning. Armed soldiers guard power stations, reservoirs and transport hubs while governments insist that recovery is still possible. Behind closed doors they are deciding who will be evacuated and who will be left behind.

You begin in 2098 as an ordinary parent trying to keep a family together during the final years of Earth.

You won’t remain that person for long.

Long Shadow is a text-first, choice-driven science-fiction RPG where you guide a single family across more than four centuries of human history. Every generation inherits the consequences of the last. Children become parents. Parents become memories. Eventually they become history.

When a character dies, the story continues through their descendants.

Your family inherits property, relationships, reputation, legal rights, unfinished disputes, old promises and forgotten mistakes. A record created during Earth’s evacuation may decide a court case two hundred years later. A law written after a desperate winter may shape an empire. Someone your family abandoned generations ago may still have descendants who remember.

There are no hero levels to grind.

There is only the family you leave behind.

A branching family saga

Long Shadow is a branching narrative RPG set in a persistent world that remembers every generation.

Guide your family through Earth’s collapse, humanity’s evacuation, life aboard Lunar Base, centuries inside a failing generation ship, the founding of New Earth and the expansion of civilisation across the stars.

Every playthrough creates a different family history.

Raise children. Build relationships. Establish settlements. Write laws. Command starships. Explore distant systems. Decide what survives each generation and what is left behind.

Governments preserve records.

Families preserve memories.

History judges both.

Earth is ending

The first decisions feel ordinary because the disaster has become routine.

Your child still goes to school. Bills still arrive. Food still needs cooking. Outside, queues grow longer every week. Water restrictions tighten. Rolling blackouts interrupt daily life. Fewer vehicles pass the house because fuel has become too valuable to waste. Military checkpoints appear around reservoirs, substations and transport routes. Everyone knows someone who has disappeared into an evacuation programme. Nobody knows how those decisions are made.

You decide what your family sees.

Do you explain what is happening, or protect your child from it for one more day?

Do you store food or help the neighbour who has already run out?

Do you keep the lights on tonight, knowing tomorrow’s electricity may cost even more?

These moments shape the household long before anyone leaves Earth.

When the evacuation begins, your family carries more than luggage.

It carries habits, trust, fear and memories that will follow every generation that comes after.

Pass through the Defence of Earth Complex

The evacuation begins long before anyone reaches a spacecraft.

Families disappear into processing centres built to move millions of people without slowing down. Every queue has a purpose. Every checkpoint produces another record. Every official decision follows your household long after Earth has been left behind.

Identity scans.

Medical examinations.

Property declarations.

Guardian verification.

Manifest interviews.

Psychological screening.

You decide what to declare, what to conceal and when to argue.

Sometimes the safest decision is to remain invisible.

Sometimes silence costs more than honesty.

Not every family reaches the next checkpoint together.

Children can be reassigned. Records can be damaged. A single disagreement may leave one parent behind while the rest of the household continues towards launch.

The people processing your family are not villains.

Most are exhausted.

Many are making impossible decisions with incomplete information.

They are trying to preserve humanity by reducing it to paperwork.

Your choices determine far more than whether you board the transport.

They establish the official version of your family’s history.

Long after the people who made those decisions are dead, later generations may still be judged by records created during a single afternoon on Earth.

Earn your place on Lunar Base

The Moon is not a sanctuary.

It is an industrial survival system where every kilogram of food, water and oxygen has already been allocated.

New arrivals become another calculation.

Every resident consumes air.

Every resident consumes water.

Every resident must justify both.

Your family receives accommodation, work assignments and education according to what Lunar administration believes you can contribute. Reputation matters. Skills matter. Official records matter.

Sometimes those records are wrong.

Work wherever the Base needs you most.

Inspect water recycling systems.

Maintain pressure doors.

Repair damaged corridors.

Audit life-support equipment.

Assist construction crews expanding new habitation blocks.

Travel into the asteroid belt to recover materials that humanity can no longer obtain from Earth.

Explore restricted archives, industrial tunnels and shipyard rings where the evacuation is quietly becoming something larger.

The Ark is already under construction.

Everyone knows there will not be enough room.

Build a future before it exists

Life on Lunar Base settles into routine, even while humanity’s future becomes less certain.

Children grow older inside steel corridors without ever seeing rain.

Families celebrate birthdays beside recycled air systems.

Neighbours disappear after reassignment.

Schools teach engineering before history because keeping the station alive matters more than remembering how civilisation ended.

Your child learns from everything around them.

Who becomes their guardian?

Which adults do they trust?

What skills do they develop?

Do they become known for solving problems, following rules or questioning authority?

The answers affect every generation that follows.

Relationships built on Lunar Base often survive longer than governments.

Some become lifelong friendships.

Some become marriages.

Some become rivalries that echo through your family for centuries.

By the time the Ark begins accepting passengers, your household has already been changed.

Not by a single dramatic event.

By thousands of ordinary decisions that slowly became permanent.

Survive the selection

Humanity cannot save everyone.

Every berth aboard the Ark has to be justified.

Families compete for space without ever seeing the calculations that decide their future. Possessions become cargo allocations. Occupations become survival scores. Entire households are reduced to numbers on a manifest that nobody is allowed to inspect.

You decide what deserves a place.

Which heirlooms remain with the family?

Which memories are worth carrying across the stars?

Who should be protected if there is only room for one more person?

The Ark was built to preserve civilisation.

It cannot preserve every life.

Live and die aboard the Ark

The voyage lasts for generations.

You will not see the destination.

Your children may not see it either.

The Ark leaves the Solar System carrying the last organised remnants of humanity. It is enormous, damaged before departure and expected to remain operational for centuries without outside support.

Soon after launch, it begins to change.

Mechanical failures isolate whole sections of the ship. Corridors close permanently. Families lose contact. Children grow up believing their compartment is the whole world.

Then life settles into routine.

People fall in love.

Children are born.

Neighbours grow old.

Someone repairs the same water pump for forty years because nobody remembers how to build another.

Children born aboard the Ark know Earth only through stories. Grandparents become photographs. Languages change. Traditions drift. Every generation inherits a ship they did not build and a destination they have never seen.

The Ark stops feeling temporary.

It becomes home.

Every generation inherits the last

Long Shadow is a generational RPG built around succession.

When your character dies, control passes to the next generation.

Your descendants inherit more than possessions.

They inherit reputation.

Old promises.

Family disputes.

Friendships.

Political enemies.

Access rights.

Property.

Professional knowledge.

Some inherit questions nobody can answer.

You might spend thirty years building trust with another household only for your grandchild to inherit the consequences of breaking it.

A decision made during childhood may still define your family two hundred years later.

Every generation begins with a history that somebody else created.

Usually you.

Build relationships that survive you

The Ark is filled with ordinary people trying to build ordinary lives inside extraordinary circumstances.

Meet engineers keeping life-support systems running beyond their design life.

Teachers trying to preserve knowledge that no longer has practical value.

Doctors working with equipment assembled from parts intended for different centuries.

Archivists deciding which memories deserve permanent space.

Children who have never seen sunlight.

Form friendships.

Find a partner.

Raise children.

Support neighbours through shortages and loss.

Attend celebrations.

Settle arguments.

Watch familiar faces disappear as time moves on and new generations take their place.

The people around your family are not temporary companions.

Many remain connected to your descendants for centuries.

Explore a living generation ship

The Ark changes as it ages.

Maintenance tunnels become neighbourhoods. Storage bays become classrooms. Engineering decks become marketplaces. Entire districts disappear behind sealed pressure doors while forgotten compartments wait decades before anyone opens them again.

Explore industrial sectors, agricultural decks, archive vaults, engineering spaces, transit systems and abandoned compartments while uncovering the history of a ship that quietly rewrites itself.

Every expedition carries risk.

Pressure doors fail without warning.

Maintenance crews vanish.

Bridges collapse.

An archive recovered after three generations may contradict everything your family believed about the voyage.

Keep the Ark alive

The Ark survives because thousands of people perform work that history rarely records.

Repair life-support systems before another compartment loses pressure. Expand hydroponics when harvests fail. Recover machinery from abandoned sections where spare parts have not been touched for generations. Restore reactors, protect water reserves and keep ageing infrastructure functioning for one more year.

Every successful repair delays another crisis.

Every neglected system becomes somebody else’s emergency.

The condition of the Ark persists across generations.

Communities remember which households kept them alive.

They also remember who chose themselves first.

The record becomes another battlefield

The longer the voyage continues, the less certain its history becomes.

Witnesses die.

Documents disappear.

Official reports contradict family journals.

Governors revise events to preserve order.

Families preserve different versions of the same disaster.

You decide what deserves to survive.

Preserve uncomfortable truths.

Destroy dangerous records.

Protect private memories.

Expose official lies.

Or allow a simpler version of history to become accepted because people need stability more than accuracy.

Future generations inherit whatever survives.

Not necessarily what happened.

Reach New Earth

Centuries after leaving Earth, the Ark finally arrives.

It does not arrive safely.

Systems fail during descent.

Compartments separate.

Landing plans collapse.

Entire sections of the ship strike the surface kilometres apart.

Families that survived the voyage may lose each other within sight of their destination.

The greatest achievement in human history ends as another struggle for survival.

The world below has no monuments waiting.

Only uncertainty.

Only opportunity.

Only the people who are still alive enough to build something from the wreckage.

Build a civilisation from the wreckage

New Earth does not begin with a victory.

It begins with survivors counting each other.

The Ark lies scattered across an unfamiliar world. Compartments have landed days apart. Cargo has been destroyed. Entire families are missing. Nobody knows how many people survived the descent.

There is no government waiting.

No established cities.

No rescue.

Only whatever your generation can build before the next winter arrives.

Recover tools. Salvage machinery. Establish shelter. Secure clean water before disease spreads. Decide how limited supplies should be shared when every choice leaves somebody without enough.

The first years are filled with practical problems.

Who receives medicine?

Who carries water?

Who records the dead?

Who settles disputes?

Those decisions stop being temporary surprisingly quickly.

Later generations simply call them tradition.

Every settlement tells a different story

Explore a new world one generation at a time.

Travel beyond the crash sites into forests, rivers, mountains and abandoned landing zones. Establish routes between isolated communities. Recover equipment from distant Ark fragments. Discover settlements founded by families who landed far from your own.

No settlement develops in the same way.

Some become centres of trade.

Some survive through engineering.

Others are built around farming, mining, archives or transport.

Each develops its own customs, priorities and version of history.

The world grows because people solve different problems in different ways.

Write the laws that future generations obey

Every society begins by solving practical problems.

Who owns recovered cargo?

Who inherits abandoned property?

Can food be stolen to save a child?

Who speaks for someone who cannot?

How should disputes be settled when nobody recognises the same authority?

Your family helps answer those questions.

Some decisions become local custom.

Others become recognised law.

Centuries later, judges may still rely on principles established during the first difficult years after landing.

A law written to survive famine may become unfair during prosperity.

A compromise accepted by one generation may burden ten more.

History rarely separates good intentions from bad outcomes.

Reputation lasts longer than memory

People remember your family.

Some remember kindness.

Others remember betrayal.

Settlements exchange stories alongside goods. Travellers carry rumours further than official reports ever could. Long after the original witnesses have died, descendants continue living with reputations they never earned.

Become known as explorers.

Builders.

Merchants.

Judges.

Engineers.

Doctors.

Or something less welcome.

A family trusted to negotiate peace may find itself expected to solve every future dispute. Another remembered for greed may discover that old accusations still close doors generations later.

Names become history long before anyone realises it.

Build a life among the stars

Humanity survives.

It expands.

New Earth becomes home, then becomes history in its own right. New settlements appear beyond the horizon. New worlds follow. Trade routes stretch between distant systems. Governments form, divide and compete. Institutions grow large enough to forget why they were created.

The problems change.

People do not.

Guide your descendants through centuries of exploration, politics, commerce and conflict as civilisation spreads beyond its first colony.

Every era introduces new opportunities, technologies, professions and challenges while preserving the consequences of everything that came before.

The family never starts again.

It only continues.

Command ships and the people aboard them

Eventually your household reaches the stars.

Purchase vessels ranging from small survey craft to heavy interstellar ships. Recruit engineers, navigators, medics, cargo specialists, security teams and civilian passengers whose experience shapes every voyage.

A ship is another community.

Crew members build friendships, hold grudges, suffer injuries, grow older and eventually retire or die. Their replacements inherit responsibilities alongside relationships that began generations earlier.

Customise propulsion, cargo systems, sensors, armour, defensive equipment and specialised modules to prepare for exploration, trade, diplomacy or dangerous expeditions beyond settled space.

Every voyage begins long before departure.

Explore, trade and negotiate

Accept contracts from governments, settlements, corporations and independent communities.

Transport vital cargo across dangerous routes. Deliver medicine before shortages become disasters. Survey unexplored systems. Recover lost vessels. Investigate abandoned stations. Negotiate access to disputed territories where diplomacy may succeed long before weapons become necessary.

The galaxy remembers reliability.

It also remembers broken promises.

Relationships built during one generation may still determine opportunities centuries later.

Combat has consequences

Conflict is dangerous because every casualty matters.

Every crew member has a purpose.

Every empty chair has a name.

Redirect power as systems begin to fail. Seal damaged compartments. Contain fires. Protect civilians. Decide whether victory is worth another life or whether retreat offers the family a future.

The fighting eventually stops.

Its consequences do not.

Ships require repairs.

Families receive casualty reports.

Trade partners lose confidence.

Political relationships deteriorate.

A battle may last twenty minutes.

Your descendants may still be living with the consequences fifty years later.

History becomes uncertain

store_data.detailed_description:
Nothing ends. It only casts a longer shadow.

Earth is dying.

Water is rationed. Fuel has become scarce. Electricity fails without warning. Armed soldiers guard power stations, reservoirs and transport hubs while governments insist that recovery is still possible. Behind closed doors they are deciding who will be evacuated and who will be left behind.

You begin in 2098 as an ordinary parent trying to keep a family together during the final years of Earth.

You won’t remain that person for long.

Long Shadow is a text-first, choice-driven science-fiction RPG where you guide a single family across more than four centuries of human history. Every generation inherits the consequences of the last. Children become parents. Parents become memories. Eventually they become history.

When a character dies, the story continues through their descendants.

Your family inherits property, relationships, reputation, legal rights, unfinished disputes, old promises and forgotten mistakes. A record created during Earth’s evacuation may decide a court case two hundred years later. A law written after a desperate winter may shape an empire. Someone your family abandoned generations ago may still have descendants who remember.

There are no hero levels to grind.

There is only the family you leave behind.

A branching family saga

Long Shadow is a branching narrative RPG set in a persistent world that remembers every generation.

Guide your family through Earth’s collapse, humanity’s evacuation, life aboard Lunar Base, centuries inside a failing generation ship, the founding of New Earth and the expansion of civilisation across the stars.

Every playthrough creates a different family history.

Raise children. Build relationships. Establish settlements. Write laws. Command starships. Explore distant systems. Decide what survives each generation and what is left behind.

Governments preserve records.

Families preserve memories.

History judges both.

Earth is ending

The first decisions feel ordinary because the disaster has become routine.

Your child still goes to school. Bills still arrive. Food still needs cooking. Outside, queues grow longer every week. Water restrictions tighten. Rolling blackouts interrupt daily life. Fewer vehicles pass the house because fuel has become too valuable to waste. Military checkpoints appear around reservoirs, substations and transport routes. Everyone knows someone who has disappeared into an evacuation programme. Nobody knows how those decisions are made.

You decide what your family sees.

Do you explain what is happening, or protect your child from it for one more day?

Do you store food or help the neighbour who has already run out?

Do you keep the lights on tonight, knowing tomorrow’s electricity may cost even more?

These moments shape the household long before anyone leaves Earth.

When the evacuation begins, your family carries more than luggage.

It carries habits, trust, fear and memories that will follow every generation that comes after.

Pass through the Defence of Earth Complex

The evacuation begins long before anyone reaches a spacecraft.

Families disappear into processing centres built to move millions of people without slowing down. Every queue has a purpose. Every checkpoint produces another record. Every official decision follows your household long after Earth has been left behind.

Identity scans.

Medical examinations.

Property declarations.

Guardian verification.

Manifest interviews.

Psychological screening.

You decide what to declare, what to conceal and when to argue.

Sometimes the safest decision is to remain invisible.

Sometimes silence costs more than honesty.

Not every family reaches the next checkpoint together.

Children can be reassigned. Records can be damaged. A single disagreement may leave one parent behind while the rest of the household continues towards launch.

The people processing your family are not villains.

Most are exhausted.

Many are making impossible decisions with incomplete information.

They are trying to preserve humanity by reducing it to paperwork.

Your choices determine far more than whether you board the transport.

They establish the official version of your family’s history.

Long after the people who made those decisions are dead, later generations may still be judged by records created during a single afternoon on Earth.

Earn your place on Lunar Base

The Moon is not a sanctuary.

It is an industrial survival system where every kilogram of food, water and oxygen has already been allocated.

New arrivals become another calculation.

Every resident consumes air.

Every resident consumes water.

Every resident must justify both.

Your family receives accommodation, work assignments and education according to what Lunar administration believes you can contribute. Reputation matters. Skills matter. Official records matter.

Sometimes those records are wrong.

Work wherever the Base needs you most.

Inspect water recycling systems.

Maintain pressure doors.

Repair damaged corridors.

Audit life-support equipment.

Assist construction crews expanding new habitation blocks.

Travel into the asteroid belt to recover materials that humanity can no longer obtain from Earth.

Explore restricted archives, industrial tunnels and shipyard rings where the evacuation is quietly becoming something larger.

The Ark is already under construction.

Everyone knows there will not be enough room.

Build a future before it exists

Life on Lunar Base settles into routine, even while humanity’s future becomes less certain.

Children grow older inside steel corridors without ever seeing rain.

Families celebrate birthdays beside recycled air systems.

Neighbours disappear after reassignment.

Schools teach engineering before history because keeping the station alive matters more than remembering how civilisation ended.

Your child learns from everything around them.

Who becomes their guardian?

Which adults do they trust?

What skills do they develop?

Do they become known for solving problems, following rules or questioning authority?

The answers affect every generation that follows.

Relationships built on Lunar Base often survive longer than governments.

Some become lifelong friendships.

Some become marriages.

Some become rivalries that echo through your family for centuries.

By the time the Ark begins accepting passengers, your household has already been changed.

Not by a single dramatic event.

By thousands of ordinary decisions that slowly became permanent.

Survive the selection

Humanity cannot save everyone.

Every berth aboard the Ark has to be justified.

Families compete for space without ever seeing the calculations that decide their future. Possessions become cargo allocations. Occupations become survival scores. Entire households are reduced to numbers on a manifest that nobody is allowed to inspect.

You decide what deserves a place.

Which heirlooms remain with the family?

Which memories are worth carrying across the stars?

Who should be protected if there is only room for one more person?

The Ark was built to preserve civilisation.

It cannot preserve every life.

Live and die aboard the Ark

The voyage lasts for generations.

You will not see the destination.

Your children may not see it either.

The Ark leaves the Solar System carrying the last organised remnants of humanity. It is enormous, damaged before departure and expected to remain operational for centuries without outside support.

Soon after launch, it begins to change.

Mechanical failures isolate whole sections of the ship. Corridors close permanently. Families lose contact. Children grow up believing their compartment is the whole world.

Then life settles into routine.

People fall in love.

Children are born.

Neighbours grow old.

Someone repairs the same water pump for forty years because nobody remembers how to build another.

Children born aboard the Ark know Earth only through stories. Grandparents become photographs. Languages change. Traditions drift. Every generation inherits a ship they did not build and a destination they have never seen.

The Ark stops feeling temporary.

It becomes home.

Every generation inherits the last

Long Shadow is a generational RPG built around succession.

When your character dies, control passes to the next generation.

Your descendants inherit more than possessions.

They inherit reputation.

Old promises.

Family disputes.

Friendships.

Political enemies.

Access rights.

Property.

Professional knowledge.

Some inherit questions nobody can answer.

You might spend thirty years building trust with another household only for your grandchild to inherit the consequences of breaking it.

A decision made during childhood may still define your family two hundred years later.

Every generation begins with a history that somebody else created.

Usually you.

Build relationships that survive you

The Ark is filled with ordinary people trying to build ordinary lives inside extraordinary circumstances.

Meet engineers keeping life-support systems running beyond their design life.

Teachers trying to preserve knowledge that no longer has practical value.

Doctors working with equipment assembled from parts intended for different centuries.

Archivists deciding which memories deserve permanent space.

Children who have never seen sunlight.

Form friendships.

Find a partner.

Raise children.

Support neighbours through shortages and loss.

Attend celebrations.

Settle arguments.

Watch familiar faces disappear as time moves on and new generations take their place.

The people around your family are not temporary companions.

Many remain connected to your descendants for centuries.

Explore a living generation ship

The Ark changes as it ages.

Maintenance tunnels become neighbourhoods. Storage bays become classrooms. Engineering decks become marketplaces. Entire districts disappear behind sealed pressure doors while forgotten compartments wait decades before anyone opens them again.

Explore industrial sectors, agricultural decks, archive vaults, engineering spaces, transit systems and abandoned compartments while uncovering the history of a ship that quietly rewrites itself.

Every expedition carries risk.

Pressure doors fail without warning.

Maintenance crews vanish.

Bridges collapse.

An archive recovered after three generations may contradict everything your family believed about the voyage.

Keep the Ark alive

The Ark survives because thousands of people perform work that history rarely records.

Repair life-support systems before another compartment loses pressure. Expand hydroponics when harvests fail. Recover machinery from abandoned sections where spare parts have not been touched for generations. Restore reactors, protect water reserves and keep ageing infrastructure functioning for one more year.

Every successful repair delays another crisis.

Every neglected system becomes somebody else’s emergency.

The condition of the Ark persists across generations.

Communities remember which households kept them alive.

They also remember who chose themselves first.

The record becomes another battlefield

The longer the voyage continues, the less certain its history becomes.

Witnesses die.

Documents disappear.

Official reports contradict family journals.

Governors revise events to preserve order.

Families preserve different versions of the same disaster.

You decide what deserves to survive.

Preserve uncomfortable truths.

Destroy dangerous records.

Protect private memories.

Expose official lies.

Or allow a simpler version of history to become accepted because people need stability more than accuracy.

Future generations inherit whatever survives.

Not necessarily what happened.

Reach New Earth

Centuries after leaving Earth, the Ark finally arrives.

It does not arrive safely.

Systems fail during descent.

Compartments separate.

Landing plans collapse.

Entire sections of the ship strike the surface kilometres apart.

Families that survived the voyage may lose each other within sight of their destination.

The greatest achievement in human history ends as another struggle for survival.

The world below has no monuments waiting.

Only uncertainty.

Only opportunity.

Only the people who are still alive enough to build something from the wreckage.

Build a civilisation from the wreckage

New Earth does not begin with a victory.

It begins with survivors counting each other.

The Ark lies scattered across an unfamiliar world. Compartments have landed days apart. Cargo has been destroyed. Entire families are missing. Nobody knows how many people survived the descent.

There is no government waiting.

No established cities.

No rescue.

Only whatever your generation can build before the next winter arrives.

Recover tools. Salvage machinery. Establish shelter. Secure clean water before disease spreads. Decide how limited supplies should be shared when every choice leaves somebody without enough.

The first years are filled with practical problems.

Who receives medicine?

Who carries water?

Who records the dead?

Who settles disputes?

Those decisions stop being temporary surprisingly quickly.

Later generations simply call them tradition.

Every settlement tells a different story

Explore a new world one generation at a time.

Travel beyond the crash sites into forests, rivers, mountains and abandoned landing zones. Establish routes between isolated communities. Recover equipment from distant Ark fragments. Discover settlements founded by families who landed far from your own.

No settlement develops in the same way.

Some become centres of trade.

Some survive through engineering.

Others are built around farming, mining, archives or transport.

Each develops its own customs, priorities and version of history.

The world grows because people solve different problems in different ways.

Write the laws that future generations obey

Every society begins by solving practical problems.

Who owns recovered cargo?

Who inherits abandoned property?

Can food be stolen to save a child?

Who speaks for someone who cannot?

How should disputes be settled when nobody recognises the same authority?

Your family helps answer those questions.

Some decisions become local custom.

Others become recognised law.

Centuries later, judges may still rely on principles established during the first difficult years after landing.

A law written to survive famine may become unfair during prosperity.

A compromise accepted by one generation may burden ten more.

History rarely separates good intentions from bad outcomes.

Reputation lasts longer than memory

People remember your family.

Some remember kindness.

Others remember betrayal.

Settlements exchange stories alongside goods. Travellers carry rumours further than official reports ever could. Long after the original witnesses have died, descendants continue living with reputations they never earned.

Become known as explorers.

Builders.

Merchants.

Judges.

Engineers.

Doctors.

Or something less welcome.

A family trusted to negotiate peace may find itself expected to solve every future dispute. Another remembered for greed may discover that old accusations still close doors generations later.

Names become history long before anyone realises it.

Build a life among the stars

Humanity survives.

It expands.

New Earth becomes home, then becomes history in its own right. New settlements appear beyond the horizon. New worlds follow. Trade routes stretch between distant systems. Governments form, divide and compete. Institutions grow large enough to forget why they were created.

The problems change.

People do not.

Guide your descendants through centuries of exploration, politics, commerce and conflict as civilisation spreads beyond its first colony.

Every era introduces new opportunities, technologies, professions and challenges while preserving the consequences of everything that came before.

The family never starts again.

It only continues.

Eventually your household reaches the stars.

Purchase vessels ranging from small survey craft to heavy interstellar ships. Recruit engineers, navigators, medics, cargo specialists, security teams and civilian passengers whose experience shapes every voyage.

A ship is another community.

Crew members build friendships, hold grudges, suffer injuries, grow older and eventually retire or die. Their replacements inherit responsibilities alongside relationships that began generations earlier.

Customise propulsion, cargo systems, sensors, armour, defensive equipment and specialised modules to prepare for exploration, trade, diplomacy or dangerous expeditions beyond settled space.

Every voyage begins long before departure.

Explore, trade and negotiate

Accept contracts from governments, settlements, corporations and independent communities.

Transport vital cargo across dangerous routes. Deliver medicine before shortages become disasters. Survey unexplored systems. Recover lost vessels. Investigate abandoned stations. Negotiate access to disputed territories where diplomacy may succeed long before weapons become necessary.

The galaxy remembers reliability.

It also remembers broken promises.

Relationships built during one generation may still determine opportunities centuries later.

Combat has consequences

Conflict is dangerous because every casualty matters.

Every crew member has a purpose.

Every empty chair has a name.

Redirect power as systems begin to fail. Seal damaged compartments. Contain fires. Protect civilians. Decide whether victory is worth another life or whether retreat offers the family a future.

Its consequences do not.

Families receive casualty reports.

Trade partners lose confidence.

Political relationships deteriorate.

Permanent Progression and Skill Tree

Unlock permanent upgrades with the experience points you gain. Gain an advantage in your next runs by boosting your starting money or base stats.

As the guillotine's blade falls, Cordelia's execution should mark the end of her story. But instead, she awakens four years in the past.

Will she become the feared villainess... or the beloved heroine? Every choice you make influences the story and its outcome.

★ Uncover the truth.

The Cult of Soren lurks beneath the cathedral, plotting in the shadows. The House of Vaelmont can never be safe until their conspiracy is brought to light.

store_data.about_the_game:
The river takes no payment in lives. Only in coin.

You drowned. Nobody found the body, nobody closed your eyes, and nobody laid the coin that pays for the crossing. So you made a bargain with Death: carry her dead, take the coin from their eyes, and one day buy your own passage.

One coin buys a crossing. One that is yours. Not given. Not taken from the dead. Earned.

Death will tell you when you have earned enough.

The dead have things to say

A hundred and forty-seven of them, muttered over the side of the boat on the way across. Nobody dies with the list finished. Some of it is funny. All of it is written down in a ledger you keep — along with everything Death has ever said to you.

It ends

Most incrementals go on forever, because forever is easier to build than an ending. TOLL is about three hours long and it finishes: there is a last purchase, a last crossing, and a last thing said to you. You can start again if you want to. You do not have to.

Five rivers, five rules

  • Styx — souls, oars, and the first skeleton who rows so you don't have to.

  • Acheron — the dead here have weight. Heavier souls pay more and sail slower.

  • Lethe — the dead here forget they are dead, and wander off your boat.

  • Phlegethon — the river burns. So does the boat.

  • Cocytus — the cold one, where the ice closes around the hull and the price is named.

The rivers talk back

Every river has a spirit who watches you work: Styx the Oath, Acheron the Woe, Lethe the Forgetting, Tisiphone the Avenger, Kokytos the Wailing. Every few minutes one of them asks you something about the life you had — a promise you broke, a thing you never finished, who you would carry first. Nothing pauses while you answer. Answer well and the river pays you better; ignore it and it doesn't. Lethe forgets your answer and asks again.

Set your own price

The river takes no payment in lives. Only in coin.

You drowned. Nobody found the body, nobody closed your eyes, and nobody laid the coin that pays for the crossing. So you made a bargain with Death: carry her dead, take the coin from their eyes, and one day buy your own passage.

One coin buys a crossing. One that is yours. Not given. Not taken from the dead. Earned.

Death will tell you when you have earned enough.

The dead have things to say

A hundred and forty-seven of them, muttered over the side of the boat on the way across. Nobody dies with the list finished. Some of it is funny. All of it is written down in a ledger you keep — along with everything Death has ever said to you.

It ends

Most incrementals go on forever, because forever is easier to build than an ending. TOLL is about three hours long and it finishes: there is a last purchase, a last crossing, and a last thing said to you. You can start again if you want to. You do not have to.

Five rivers, five rules

  • Styx — souls, oars, and the first skeleton who rows so you don't have to.

  • Acheron — the dead here have weight. Heavier souls pay more and sail slower.

  • Lethe — the dead here forget they are dead, and wander off your boat.

Every river has a spirit who watches you work: Styx the Oath, Acheron the Woe, Lethe the Forgetting, Tisiphone the Avenger, Kokytos the Wailing. store_data.about_the_game:
Blackforest

Will you escape... or become part of the basement?

You wake up on the cold floor of a dark underground basement. Your head is pounding, your memories are blurred, and every door is locked. Somewhere within the maze of narrow corridors, the man who brought you here is still searching.

There is only one way out.

Explore the sprawling basement, uncover hidden objects, decipher codes, and solve puzzles as you fight your way toward freedom. But be careful—every mistake could be your last.

The killer relentlessly patrols the dark hallways. If you hear his footsteps, hide immediately and stay as quiet as possible. If he finds you, there won't be a second chance.

With an average playtime of around one hour, Blackforest delivers an intense first-person horror experience focused on suspense, atmosphere, and psychological tension. Featuring a grounded, realistic story with no supernatural elements, every decision matters as the constant feeling of being hunted never lets up.

Features

  • Explore an atmospheric basement filled with hidden secrets.

  • Solve puzzles and decipher codes to unlock new areas.

  • Collect important items and piece together crucial clues.

  • Hide from the killer and move silently through the darkness.

  • Immersive first-person horror with a realistic atmosphere.

  • Approximately 1 hour of gameplay.

  • One ending — every encounter with the killer could end your escape.
