store_data.about_the_game:
One kitchen. Ten hours. Four cooks who won't stop moving the stove.

Tiny Chef is a co-op restaurant management game. You open the doors, customers sit down, and from that moment you are behind. Chop, fry, plate, run it to the table, take the next order on the way back. Somewhere in there the fryer catches fire and nobody has washed a plate since Tuesday.

Play alone, on one couch, or online with up to four people.

The shift

Every day runs on a real clock. Demand rises and falls with the hour, so the lunch rush is a different game than the dead stretch at 3pm. Customers arrive alone or in parties of up to four, sit together, order together, and lose patience together. Serve the table late and the whole party walks.

Nothing about the kitchen is fixed. Pick up the chopping board and carry it somewhere better. Buy a second stove off your phone and wait two days for the truck. Fires spread to the next counter if you don't get there in time.

The rest of the day

The shift is only part of it. Between services you drive back to HQ, sleep until whatever hour you choose, and spend the money you made:

  • Order appliances and gadgets by phone and unload the delivery truck yourself

  • Learn new dishes and decide which ones stay on the menu

  • Run ad campaigns to pull in more customers than you can handle

  • Hire contractors to knock out walls, move doors and rebuild the floor plan

  • Buy the empty lot next door and grow the building into it

  • Book a cleaning crew when you really do not want to face the sink

Do well enough and you open a second restaurant. Then a third. Fail enough orders in one day and the health inspector shuts one down, and reopening costs more the longer you've been running.

Your cook is yours

Make a character, pick their face and clothes, and take them anywhere. Skills go from 1 to 99 and only go up by doing the work. Chop a thousand onions and you chop faster. Fight enough fires and you stop being scared of the fryer. Your  character carries that progress into any save and into anyone else's game.

Co-op that actually shares the kitchen

Online through Steam, or two players on one screen with controllers. Everyone cooks, everyone can buy things, everyone can move the furniture while you're standing on it. There is one phone and whoever grabbed it first is using it.

Also, there is a bed and a car

You have to drive to work. You have to sleep. You will, at some point, open the restaurant and immediately be told you cannot start the shift because there is one dirty plate on a table. That one is on you.

store_data.about_the_game:
A package was delivered to your house by mistake. The address on the package is in another country, so you set out to return it in person, well, in dog (you are a dog).

The country turns out to be a strange place. People (dogs) there settle everything with target-shooting duels. Nobody finds this odd except you.

The trick is the ricochet: bullets bounce off walls, so the best shots are the ones that look impossible until they land. Hitting targets shakes your opponent's confidence.

Along the way you travel with a cat who was raised by dogs and firmly believes she is one. You meet the locals, run into trouble, help random grandma, and sort most of it out with a well-placed bank shot.

Features

  • A very fun story

  • Meet random dogs (well, mostly) along the way

  • Pretty scene

  • Full controller support

  • Interesting levels

store_data.about_the_game:
Books for Bad Neighbors

It's 199X. This is the only bookshop for forty miles, and you work the counter now. The register is old, the computer screen glows orange, and the mail comes every day whether you want it or not.

A priest hears the confession. A doctor sees the wound. You get a list of what they read at two in the morning, and it tells you more than both of them put together.

The work is simple

Order new books every day. Read the letters. Find the books you have. Pack the boxes. Hit your quota, close the shop. Then do it again tomorrow.

What the supplier sells changes every week, and some books sell out and never come back, so what you can give people is not always your choice.

Fill enough orders for one person and their letters get longer. They start telling you things. By then you've read enough of their mail to finish their sentences.

Some orders you should not fill

You still have a quota to hit, and if you say no to someone, they will want to know why, and they know where you work.

The shop closes at six. You walk home the same way every night.

Features

  • Multiple mysteries to uncover, one order at a time

  • Different endings based on what you sold and who you sold it to

  • Everything happens on the shop computer, built to feel like a real 199X machine

store_data.about_the_game:
Miners, Moos & Miracles is an idle/incremental farm-and-adventure game with a retro CRT-styled shell.

Start with a modest homestead and watch gold, barley, milk, and eggs roll in while you're away. Reinvest your earnings, then step through the door into a handful of wildly different mini-games, all set in the same strange little world:

  • Dark Mine — send your miners underground to battle demons for shards, upgrading equipment, dynamite, and hydraulics along the way.

  • Cooking — combine eggs, milk, seeds, fish, and a few less wholesome ingredients into dozens of recipes, from a Simple Stew to a full-blown Reincarnation Ritual.

  • Cow Ball — the barnyard's favorite sport. Exactly what it sounds like.

  • Chicken Coop — keep the flock happy, then fend off egg-snatching UFOs in the coop's Space Invasion mode.

  • Aquarium — feed and grow fish in the homestead.

  • Wardrobe — customize your character's look.

When you've pushed as far as you can, Rebirth: reset your progress for a permanent bonus, a growing skill tree, and a merchant who'll trade your hard-earned resources for Prestige Points.

Over 50 achievements track your progress across every resource and mini-game plus a few one-off moments worth catching, if you're paying attention.

Feature list

  • Idle/incremental homestead management: miners, farms, houses, cows, and more

  • Six distinct mini-games in one shared world: Dark Mine, Cooking, Cow Ball, Chicken Coop, Aquarium, and Wardrobe

  • A full Rebirth/Prestige system with a skill tree and permanent bonuses

  • Over 50 Steam achievements, from resource milestones to one-off surprises

  • A retro CRT-styled UI shell with scanlines, bezel themes, and screen effects

store_data.about_the_game:
Let Go of That Throat Cover is a free visual novel set in a near-modern world with reversed gender expectations. Men are expected to hide their Adam's apples with throat covers and to be gentle, pale, delicate, and obedient, while women hold the dominant social position.

You play an ordinary office worker who is pulled into this gender-reversed world and meets four male leads: Gu Lian, Li Ruoxi, Feng Tiantian, and Shen Wei. Your choices shape affection, hidden variables, routes, and endings as the romantic comedy gradually reveals something strange beneath everyday life.

Features:

  • Gender-role reversal worldbuilding built around romance, social satire, and everyday absurdity.

  • Four main romance routes with different personalities and relationship dynamics.

  • Choice-driven story progress with affection changes, hidden variables, saves, character portraits, CGs, and background music.

  • Multiple endings, including route endings, bad endings, and clues toward a deeper hidden truth.

The game contains satire, romance, comedy, and light social themes, but no explicit adult content.

Package Chaos is a cozy package sorting game where you turn a messy warehouse into a perfectly organized delivery center.

Pick up, inspect, and sort thousands of unique packages by their size, colors, logos, labels, and special handling marks. Discover matching items, create neat stacks, and bring order to the chaos.

Sort. Stack. Satisfy.

store_data.about_the_game:
Dunjin

The Dunjin. You'd heard the name whispered. Heard the stories. But nothing prepared you for what waits in the dark - something old, something patient, something that's spent centuries reshaping the world above it to its will. Every floor you descend, you feel it. Watching. Waiting. And now it knows you're coming.

Play your hand, then roll your fate

Dunjin fuses poker-hand deckbuilding with dice-driven dungeon crawling. Build hands from a deck of sigil-marked cards to generate Mana and Mult, then let the d20 decide whether your hit lands, fumbles, or strikes for a crit. Your cards are only half the story down here, but they can easily make or break your run. Here's how it works.

Four sigils, one descent

Every card bears one of four sigils - Divine, Arcane, Martial, and Shadow - each enabling different strategies and synergies in battle. Divine heals you up, Arcane breaks shields, Martial melts HP, and Shadow shreds armor.

Damage is compounded by the strength of your hand. Rig the deck towards your favourite sigil, the relics you find, or even a hand type you have a keen eye for (looking at you, flushmaxxers).

24 classes: no two runs alike

From the stalwart Knight to the humble Rat King, every hero descends with a different set of perks and passives. Some load the dice, others rig the deck. No two heroes play the same, and each one is uniquely equipped to get you the upper-hand on your journey.

Dungeons with stories untold

Chart your path down a branching map of battles, shops, treasures, random encounters and campfires. 50+ different storyline threads weave through your runs, and the choices you make in the early floors echo as you make your way down.

Endless replayability

With a Scrapbook full of discoveries waiting to be made, Dunjin is a completionist's paradise. Track the progress you've made both per hero and across them all, with up to 5 save slots letting you play alongside family and friends. With 2.8 trillion seeds and a built-in seed finder, there are endless dungeons to conquer. Be the first to find the best.

Explore the depths

Think your build is broken? Finish the descent and conquer the boss to unlock Endless mode. Tackle loop after loop of hardcore enemies and see how far your relics can take you.

The highlights

  • Poker-hand scoring meets dungeon-themed d20 combat

  • 24 playable classes with unique decks, mechanics and gameplay loops

  • 200+ relics, potions, and card enhancements

  • Branching maps with events, shops, battles, and storyline threads

  • 2.8 trillion unique seeds - share your favourites and tackle them with friends

  • Endless mode, cosmetics, an unlockable sandbox, and collection/scrapbook tracking to track progress

  • Original procedural soundtrack

Higher-level characters overpower lower-level ones.

Short on gold and want to power up fast? Come try your luck at the casino!

Bet on which side will win – if you win, you’ll quickly accumulate funds.

Skill: Deal true damage when have shielded.

Gear: Increase attack speed on each hit.

Class upgrade: Transform a character into an ‘Etherborn,’ gaining a shield equal to max HP at the start of battle.

Combine two Star-grade characters to create a Moon-grade characters, and two Moon-grade characters to create a Sun-grade characters.

Come collect characters, build your own lineup, and explore the Aether world!

store_data.about_the_game:
Descend. Loot. Escape — or lose it all.

Depths of Providence is a roguelike JRPG inspired by the Ancient Cave of Lufia II. Every run drops your four-hero party at floor 1, level 1, with nothing but the relics you've banked from previous descents. One hundred procedurally generated floors stand between you and the Guardian of the Depths. What you carry out is yours forever, but only if you make it out.

Every run is a gamble. Red chests hold run-only gear, consumables, and spell scrolls to keep you alive right now. Blue chests hold rare named equipment; escape with them and they're banked in your vault forever, ready at the start of every future run. Somewhere on floors 15–24, a single glowing Providence chest lets you end the run from anywhere and keep everything you've found. Cash out early and bank little, or push deeper and risk it all. Die, and everything you found this run is gone.

The deep floors are unfair on purpose. Instant-death gazes, petrification, and full-party nukes await the greedy. Death wards, white magic, and knowing when to run are the difference between a full vault and an empty one. Every tenth floor a mini-boss guards the stairs, and floor 100 belongs to Chrono-Lord Aiful himself: slay him and your haul is banked and forged into a super-blue, a relic with a unique, randomly generated affix all your own.

Secrets run deeper still. Rumor speaks of eight Ancient Key shards scattered through blue chests. Complete the key and bring it to the cave's depths, and something older opens

Compete on the Daily. Everyone descends the same seeded cave each day. Same floors, same chests, same formations, and races for depth on a global leaderboard. Every run is replay-verified, so the board is real.

Features:

  • 100 procedurally generated floors with escalating, deliberately punishing depths

  • Persistent vault: bank rare blue-chest relics across every future run

  • The Providence mechanic: a genuine risk/reward "cash out or push on" decision every run

  • Turn-based JRPG battle with classes, spells, elemental affinities, and 11 equipment slots

  • Named super-blue relics forged with unique procedural affixes

  • Hidden Ancient Key questline and an unlockable custom Party Builder

  • Daily seeded runs with a global, replay-verified leaderboard

  • Full controller support, Steam Deck ready

A Personal Note from the Developer:

The above is all accurate, but it's ostensibly the typical marketing hype one might read for a game. I wanted to tell you the brutally honest truth about why I made this game, and why I think you might enjoy it. I really enjoy JRPG's. My biggest complaint about them has always been that they're too easy. Some might have moments that are challenging, others may start a bit difficult but pretty soon the player just stat checks everything and it's a snooze. The game I always have wanted is a turn based JRPG with a high skill cap, near infinite replayability, and a competitive aspect. That game, as far as I am aware, does not exist, so I set out to make it.

The story mode of the game is cool. One basically tries to go as deep as possible to acquire as many powerful blue chest items as they can before they escape the Depths via Providence. There's real tension between pushing deeper or getting out with what you can. The player is not supposed to make it to floor 100 on the first run. I think this mode is fun, but it isn't really the primary mode I built this game for, though if you are someone who loves meta-progression, stacking mountains of obscenely powerful items, then you might love this mode forever.

The other mode is the daily challenge run. This run has no meta-progression. You start from level 1 on floor 1 with no skills and no banked items. You and everyone else face the same procedurally generated Depths on any given day; same enemy formations, same chest contents, same skill drops, and same blue chest items. This mode is fine-tuned with increased blue chest occurrence such that with near perfect play, and a little bit of luck, a player might hope to make it deep, but the overwhelming majority of players will probably die off at floor 20-something. There's a daily leaderboard to track who makes it the deepest on any given day and there's server side replay validation of every submitted run so that players can be assured of fair play. This mode is why I built this game, and I promise to always tune this to be fiendishly difficult so that if you can pull off a deep run, it'll be something to really be proud of.

Anyway, I truly hope you enjoy this game as much as I do. I'm honestly not expecting huge commercial success from this endeavor; I just want to share my work with others in the hopes that some of you might enjoy the game as much as I do. My heartfelt thanks for considering purchasing my game.

store_data.about_the_game:
Stop time. Hang the bullets. Remember to step aside.

You're the only thing moving in a frozen world. A bullet hovers eight inches from your face. A grenade sits motionless mid-arc. A crowd of dummies stands there, mouths open - and you have all the time in the world to decide what happens to them.

Shoot, and your bullets hang in the air. Throw grenades, and they stay exactly where you left them. Shove enemies around, line them up in each other's crossfire, tuck their own explosives back into their hands. Then let time run - and watch it all happen at once.

You're not hitting pause. You're staging a scene.

Freezing time isn't a breather here, it's a director's chair. Build a thirty-bullet volley. Rig a chain reaction: bullet hits boulder, boulder launches a dummy, dummy sails into a crowd with a grenade already waiting in it. Unfreezing time is your "Action!"

And yes, you're standing right in the middle of it.

This is a first-person shooter, and your body is part of the plan. The bullet you parked by the doorway doesn't care who parked it there. The shockwave you forgot to hide behind will find you first. Before you let time run, there's one question left: where do you stand to survive your own masterpiece?

Your dummies come straight out of myth

Sling-swinging satyrs. Harpies raining feather-darts mid-dive. Cyclopes lobbing smoldering boulders. Bronze guardians behind tower shields. A gorgon whose gaze petrifies anything it lands on - including her own allies, if you nudge them into the beam. And eventually, you'll meet the ones who can stop time too. That's when it becomes a real duel.

What's inside:

  • Sandbox - one arena, the full arsenal, zero rules. Build Rube Goldberg machines, shoot movies, break physics.

  • Challenges - dozens of levels with brutal conditions: one bullet for five enemies, one freeze for the whole level, everyone dies in a single volley.

  • Style scoring - shooting a dummy point-blank earns you nothing. A five-link chain, an enemy killed by his own redirected bullet, a kill pulled off an inch from your own death - that earns you everything.

  • Replays - every cascade is recorded and replayed from a free camera. The first time you'll see yourself from the outside, standing in the middle of the hell you built. One click to save the clip.

  • Ragdolls, explosions, and a total absence of dignity - the dummies have none. Neither will you, when the plan goes wrong.

Time is stopped. The bullets are waiting. Sure you thought this through?

store_data.about_the_game:
A mysterious corruption is spreading across the region, twisting the minds of every creature it touches. Assemble a team of animal survivors, uncover the source behind the outbreak, and fight your way through ever-changing runs where every battle, card and Artifact shapes your strategy.

Command Three Survivors

Every battle is fought by a team of three survivors, each with their own deck, strengths and combat role. The entire party shares a single Action Point pool, so every card played is a choice between offense, defense and supporting your teammates. Success comes from coordinating the whole team rather than relying on a single character.

Every Character Brings a Different Strategy

Each survivor contributes to the team in a different way. Sharp Bengal overwhelms enemies with relentless offense, Pirate Albino supports the fight through gadgets and calculated precision, while Boss Shepherd keeps the team alive with powerful defensive abilities. Experiment with different team compositions to discover powerful strategies that no single character could achieve alone.

Survive the Corruption

The corruption is as dangerous as the enemies themselves. Each survivor has a Stagger meter. When it fills, they become Broken, losing their next turn and becoming vulnerable to devastating attacks. Most defensive cards allow another survivor to Intercept an incoming attack, stepping in to take the hit instead. Knowing when to protect an ally—and when to risk pushing forward—can decide the outcome of an entire battle.

Build Three Decks

Each survivor builds their own deck throughout the run. Draft new cards, upgrade existing ones and discover powerful Artifacts that reshape your strategy. Every addition strengthens an individual character while creating new synergies across the entire team, making every run feel different.

Explore a Corrupted Region

Travel through corrupted Zones filled with dangerous enemies, unpredictable Events, powerful Elites and terrifying Bosses. Every route presents different risks and rewards, encouraging you to adapt your strategy as the corruption grows stronger.

store_data.about_the_game:
Ascend the Pixel Dungeon is a turn-based dungeon crawler.

The controls feel familiar — but this is not a game about picking a class tree and growing into it. You define how you fight with spellbooks, reshape your body with factors, and let maps and choices split every run apart.

The first door does not always open onto the same sewers. Some runs begin in a humid jungle. Segmented monsters that choke corridors, theme bosses at the end of a biome, spellbooks from bosses and chests — the question becomes which book you push for this time.

Defeat monsters and you may find factors. Absorb them and adaptations take hold. These are not simple stat buffs. Vision, hunger, equipment limits, and combat rules change — how your body lives in the dungeon changes. If spellbooks are how you fight, adaptations are the body that endures that fight.

Between chapters, a bonfire waits. Combine materials. Choose a material and forge weapons and armor. Start as a race — human or gnoll — face monsters that wear gear, and turn what they drop into the next decision.

Each run splits along those lines: starting biome, books in hand, body you absorbed, materials you forged. Learn the rules once. Become a different body the next time.

Key Features

• Turn-based pixel-art dungeon crawling — one tile, one action

• Spellbook-driven builds — carry books in a run and invest level-up points into them

• Factors & adaptations — kill monsters, learn their bodies

• Runs that diverge from the start — sewers or jungle

• Theme bosses and guaranteed or random spellbooks — the nameplate of your strategy

• Bonfire crafting — recipes and material-based forging

• Race select — human or gnoll as different starting bodies

• Equipped monsters — tougher fights, drops that matter

Ascend the Pixel Dungeon is a fork built on Shattered Pixel Dungeon. The bones of the controls are familiar. The axes of growth and run divergence are rebuilt.

@AI is used in art, music, and code.

store_data.about_the_game:
YOU ARE THE LEVEL

You are a drop of living ink, and everywhere you go, you leave a line. Not a pretty trail effect — a wall. Solid, permanent, and entirely your fault.

Jump a gap and you've drawn a ramp you can land on later. Fall down a shaft and you've split the room in two. Grab that shiny collectible without thinking, and congratulations: you've inked yourself into a corner with no way out. In DEADLINE, every level is solvable — but only if you plan your entire path like a single, continuous pen stroke.

DRAW YOUR WAY OUT

  • Your past is the architecture. Land on your own arcs, wall-jump off your own mistakes, knit ladders out of your falls.

  • One gap in the stroke. The Pen Lift lets you dash without drawing — once. Where you choose not to leave a mark is the whole puzzle.

  • Think first, execute second. Deaths teach routing, not reflexes. When you fail, it won't be your thumbs — it'll be that beautiful prison you built for yourself.

BEWARE THE RED PEN

The page fights back. Crosshatched spikes, strike-through lines, and stamped X's — every hazard is an editor's correction mark, and the Red Pen itself hunts anything that colors outside the lines. Solvent pools dissolve your ink. Fresh pages wipe the slate. Use them, or drown in your own handwriting.

ELEGANCE IS THE HIGH SCORE

You're not graded on speed. You're graded on ink. Every level scores your total stroke length — the shortest, cleanest line takes the gold. Finish a level and see your entire run framed as a single drawing: your solution, signed and hung on the wall. No two players draw the same picture.

  • 30+ hand-inked levels across notebook, graph paper, and aged parchment

  • A stroke-length medal system that rewards elegance over reflexes

  • Instant restarts, single-screen puzzles, zero filler

  • A living pen-on-paper art style where the whole world is hand-drawn — including by you

Solve it like a puzzle. Execute it like a speedrun. Frame it like art.

store_data.about_the_game:
Aircraft Tycoon is a strategy and management simulation game where you build and grow an aircraft manufacturing company from the pioneering age of aviation.

Begin with a small operation, limited resources, and early technology. Design aircraft, build prototypes, conduct tests, present your models to the market, and turn commercial opportunities into real orders.

BUILD YOUR AIRCRAFT COMPANY

Start with a modest worksite and gradually expand your company’s capabilities. Manage facilities, finances, aircraft models, contracts, suppliers, and production capacity.

DESIGN AND DEVELOP AIRCRAFT

Create aircraft by combining airframes, wings, engines, flight control systems, fuel systems, equipment packages, and landing gear.

Every decision affects performance, cost, reliability, safety, production difficulty, and how well the aircraft meets the needs of the market.

BUILD AND TEST PROTOTYPES

Turn your designs into working prototypes. Conduct ground tests, complete the first flight, and run flight test campaigns to identify technical limitations and validate each aircraft model.

Choose whether to correct problems, accept limitations, invest in further development, or redesign the aircraft.

PRESENT YOUR AIRCRAFT TO THE MARKET

Organize market demonstrations, attract potential customers, and evaluate commercial interest in your aircraft.

Different customers value different qualities, including price, reliability, performance, delivery time, and operational suitability.

NEGOTIATE ORDERS AND MANAGE CONTRACTS

Respond to commercial enquiries and define prices, quantities, and delivery schedules.

Promising more than your company can deliver may win an order in the short term, but delays and failures can damage your finances, customer relationships, and reputation.

SOURCE ENGINES AND MANAGE SUPPLIERS

Purchase engines from external suppliers, compare available offers, place priority orders, track deliveries, and manage engine inventory across your worksites.

Supplier availability, prices, and delivery times can directly affect aircraft design and production planning.

MANAGE PRODUCTION AND DELIVERY

Prepare production, allocate capacity, control costs, and manufacture aircraft for active contracts.

Successful deliveries generate revenue and strengthen your reputation. Poor planning, shortages, or unrealistic deadlines can threaten both the contract and the future of the company.

BUILD A COMPANY THAT CAN SURVIVE THE HISTORY OF AVIATION

Aircraft Tycoon is not a flight simulator. It is a business and industrial management game about technology, risk, markets, production, finance, and the long-term decisions required to build a successful aircraft manufacturer.

store_data.about_the_game:
LEAD · EXPLORE · CRAFT · BUILD · RESEARCH · TRADE · FIGHT

At the dawn of civilization, there are no safe borders, no roads to follow, and no future you can take for granted. There is only a small tribe, an uncharted land, and a leader whose choices will shape the fate of generations.

Stone to Stars is a colony sim and ruler simulator set at the dawn of civilization. Settle an uncharted continent, build a thriving settlement, discover new technologies, trade or wage war with your neighbors—and hold on to power as you guide your dynasty through the ages.

LEAD

You do not rule over a faceless colony, but a living society. Your people will follow you only as long as they trust your judgment and believe you can safeguard their future.

Endure crises, meet the needs of your tribe, and maintain the support of your people. Lose their trust, and you may be overthrown—and defeated.

But even the most successful reign must eventually end. Guide your dynasty, prepare worthy successors, and pass power into their hands so that what you began may endure for generations.

EXPLORE

At the start of each game, choose the continent on which your civilization’s story will unfold. Every continent has its own landscapes, climate, resources, and neighboring settlements.

Send your people into the unknown, reveal the map, locate sources of food and raw materials, choose where to expand, and discover who else lays claim to these lands.

CRAFT

Gather resources, hunt wildlife, process what you bring home, and turn natural materials into tools, weapons, clothing, and supplies.

Resources are not abstract numbers: they must be gathered, processed, carried, stored, and delivered wherever they are needed. Every item becomes part of your settlement’s physical economy.

BUILD

Begin with a single campfire and temporary shelters, then transform your settlement into a thriving state with homes, workshops, storehouses, farmland, and infrastructure.

Assign workers, organize logistics, and establish production chains. Resources will not move on their own, and every decision has consequences.

RESEARCH

Accumulate knowledge and choose your path of development. A branching technology tree unlocks new materials, crafts, gathering methods, buildings, and ways to organize your society.

Lead your people from the first stone tools into new eras. Every discovery reshapes life in your settlement and opens new possibilities for your civilization.

TRADE OR FIGHT

You are not alone on your chosen continent. Other settlements are autonomous, AI-controlled societies. They grow, explore the land, gather resources, and pursue goals of their own.

Exchange goods, cooperate, and preserve the peace—or exert pressure, defend your territory, and go to war. Relationships are shaped by your actions, so today’s trading partner may become tomorrow’s enemy.

FACE THE FINAL TRIAL

The growth of your civilization is not the only goal. Hidden within every game is an inevitable final trial that will demand everything your people have achieved across the generations.

Your accumulated knowledge, stockpiles, production chains, relationships with neighboring societies, and the consequences of generations of decisions will all shape the final struggle for the future. Only a civilization that has prepared for what lies ahead will be able to save its people and carry their story beyond the world they have always known.

Only then will you discover whether you have built a civilization capable of enduring through the ages—or one destined to vanish alongside all the rest.

Exchange goods, cooperate, and preserve the peace—or exert pressure, defend your territory, and go to war. Relationships are shaped by your actions, so today’s trading partner may become tomorrow’s enemy.

The growth of your civilization is not the only goal. Hidden within every game is an inevitable final trial that will demand everything your people have achieved across the generations.

Your accumulated knowledge, stockpiles, production chains, relationships with neighboring societies, and the consequences of generations of decisions will all shape the final struggle for the future. Only a civilization that has prepared for what lies ahead will be able to save its people and carry their story beyond the world they have always known.

Only then will you discover whether you have built a civilization capable of enduring through the ages—or one destined to vanish alongside all the rest.

store_data.about_the_game:
【Inherit the Archive of Fate, Forgotten by the World】

You were once an ordinary person living on Earth.

An unexpected crossing carries you into a world where gods, spirits, Sequences, and supernatural powers are all real. You belong to no faction, possess no inherited bloodline, and are bound by neither a predetermined Sequence nor an established fate. For that very reason, an ancient existence that has lain dormant for centuries chooses you—the Archive of Fate.

Once, its halls preserved countless bodies of knowledge, rituals, potion formulas, and Sequence legacies. Complete records of all twenty-two Major Arcana paths could be found within its collection.

Now, its treasures have been scattered and every former heir has vanished. The only presence left to answer you is the Afterglow—a fading consciousness with fractured memories and dwindling power.

And you are the Archive of Fate’s sole and final heir.

【Prepare, Embark, and Venture Forth Again】

The game revolves around two interconnected phases: preparing at home and embarking on randomized expeditions.

Organize your deck and inventory → Choose a region → Traverse a randomized map → Face battles and events → Collect cards and materials → Return home → Brew potions → Advance your Sequence → Set out once more

At home, you can refine your deck, manage your inventory and attributes, study alchemical formulas, and plan around the region, time of day, and weather conditions ahead.

Every expedition generates a brand-new side-scrolling map. Choose your path between battles, random events, shops, treasures, rest sites, and formidable enemies as you gather experience, cards, gold, materials, and forgotten knowledge.

Pressing deeper promises greater rewards—but also deadlier threats. Returning before it is too late allows you to preserve your gains, adjust your build, research new formulas, and prepare for the next journey.

【Wield a Variety of Cards and All 56 Minor Arcana】

Tarot is not mere decoration. It is woven directly into the rules of combat and progression.

You can wield a wide variety of cards and build your deck around the complete set of 56 Minor Arcana. Wands, Cups, Swords, and Pentacles each possess distinct elemental affinities, tactical roles, and symbolic meanings.

Every Minor Arcana card has both an Upright and a Reversed form. These two forms accumulate Attunement independently, advance through separate growth stages, and gradually unlock new branches of effects.

The same card may grant empowering possibilities in one form while revealing a dangerous shadow in the other. To truly master a Tarot card is to understand—and wield—every side of its nature.

【Choose from Twenty-Two Major Arcana Sequences】

Your journey does not always begin with the Fool.

Because you come from another world, you are unbound by its established Sequence system and the karmic ties of its past. This allows you to carry the destinies of different—and sometimes even contradictory—Major Arcana.

You may choose your first path from twenty-two Major Arcana Sequences.

The Fool embodies the unknown, adventure, and limitless possibility. The Magician represents creation, communication, and skill. The High Priestess leads toward wisdom, intuition, and hidden truths. The Emperor pursues order and dominion. Death signifies endings, transformation, and rebirth...

Every Sequence offers its own abilities, potions, rituals, methods of embodiment, and conditions for advancement.

Choosing a Sequence is more than choosing a class.

You must understand it, live by it, and gradually become the archetype embodied by that Major Arcana.

Until at last, you ascend to godhood.

【Freeform Alchemy and Sequence Advancement】

In this world, potions are the path through which mortals enter the supernatural Sequences.

Materials gathered during expeditions possess different elements, medicinal properties, qualities, hidden traits, and potential substitutes.

You are free to select your ingredients and precisely adjust their quantities. Discover synergistic combinations, avoid conflicting properties, or experiment in hopes of triggering unknown effects. The outcome of each brew may also be influenced by the time, weather, location, and your level of alchemical mastery.

Official formulas provide reliable guidance, but they are not necessarily the only—or best—solutions. Through repeated experimentation and careful record-keeping, you can discover superior combinations, uncover hidden proportions, and preserve formulas of your own creation.

Experience and levels are only prerequisites for advancement.

To rise to a higher Sequence, you must also brew and consume the corresponding potion, embody the principles of your path, and complete its required advancement ritual.

Power is never a gift without a price.

The wrong ingredients or proportions may weaken a potion, build up toxicity, waste precious resources, or even cause the drinker to gradually lose their sense of self.

【Ascend to Godhood Twenty-Two Times】

To restore the Archive of Fate, all twenty-two divine seats of the Major Arcana must be recorded once again.

In the past, each seat belonged to a different godlike being. Now, only one heir remains. You must therefore walk all twenty-two Sequences alone.

Choose a Major Arcana Sequence, begin at Sequence 9, and progress through growth, embodiment, potions, and advancement rituals until you finally ascend to godhood.

Whenever you complete a Sequence, the Archive of Fate permanently records its corresponding divine seat.

You must then willingly relinquish the power you have just obtained, fall from godhood back into mortality, and begin the next path at Sequence 9.

The Archive can ensure that surrendering your divinity will not kill you. It cannot spare you from the growth, potions, rituals, and sacrifices required afterward.

You will never wield twenty-two divine powers at once.

What you gain instead is the experience of reaching the summit twenty-two times—and surrendering everything by your own hand each time.

【The Expedition Ends, but Your Legacy Remains】

A single expedition may come to an end, but your growth and legacy will not be erased.

Experience, gold, card collections, Attunement, materials, formulas, abilities, and discovered knowledge all carry over into your long-term progression.

You may continue developing the deck formed during your expedition, or rebuild it entirely and begin your next journey with a completely different strategy.

When you ascend through a Sequence and willingly relinquish its divinity, the corresponding divine seat is permanently preserved within the Archive of Fate.

Expeditions strengthen your character. The Sequence cycle gradually restores the Archive itself.

【Uncover the Truth Behind the Archive’s Fall】

How did the Archive of Fate fall from the greatest supernatural power in the world to a name almost no one remembers?

The Afterglow tells you that the former Keeper once reached Sequence 1 of the World Sequence. Only one final step remained before ascending to godhood and awakening the supreme treasure hidden deep within the Archive.

But word of this achievement was somehow leaked. The Keeper was betrayed and attacked, losing control at the final moment. The Archive of Fate fell into decline soon afterward.

Yet this is not the whole truth.

Who leaked the secret?

Who was truly responsible for the attack?

Why did the Keeper lose control at the final moment?

Have the Afterglow’s memories been altered?

Was the Archive of Fate the victim of a catastrophe—or the force that caused one?

The Afterglow is your first mentor.

It is also a narrator whose every claim must be verified by you.

【Three Wishes】

Deep within the Archive of Fate lies a dormant treasure said to be capable of granting three wishes.

Only after all twenty-two divine seats of the Major Arcana have been recorded can it truly awaken.

The first wish has already been written into the covenant of inheritance: restore the Archive of Fate and return this ancient power, forgotten by the world, to its former glory.

The other two wishes belong to you.

You may use them to return to Earth, undo the regrets of your past, reshape this world, or establish a future entirely different from the Archive of old.

But after ascending to godhood, relinquishing everything, and beginning again twenty-two times, will you still remain the person you once were?

Should you restore the Archive of Fate as it existed in the past—or create a new age defined by your own choices?

When every thread of fate converges, the true question may not be what your wishes can accomplish, but—

【What do you ultimately wish to become?】

store_data.about_the_game:
FLOPPY SURVIVORS is a bullet heaven roguelite about one tiny floppy disk against an entire corrupted network. Stack auto-firing antivirus weapons, survive endless malware hordes, complete recovery jobs, and fuse pairs into devastating DUAL weapons.


You're DISK #47, and the network wants you deleted. The question is... why?





Deleting malware is just survival; repairing the system is your true objective. Completing tasks visually restores the battlefield and grants massive upgrades:


  • Stabilize damaged sectors.
  • Close numbered ports.
  • Seal quarantine nodes.

Survive long enough to delete all 10 bosses, then hold the FINAL DEFRAG core for 60 seconds to win.





Inventory space is tight, but fusion is your way out. Upgrade two programs to Lv. 5 to fuse them into a massive DUAL weapon, freeing up a slot for even more firepower. Experiment with combinations, discover the hidden synergies, and save every successful build into your permanent DUAL.DAT archive.



CRACK CACHES, UPGRADE, SURVIVE


Deleting a boss cracks open its cache, rewarding you with one POWER DRIVER and two instant skill upgrades. Customize your build on the fly:


  • Push damage into overdrive.
  • Speed up system recovery.
  • Reshape movement and blink timing.

DECRYPT THE MYSTERY


Defeating bosses across all difficulties unlocks 30 unique INTERCEPT signals. Every victory permanently strengthens your build while piecing together another fragment of the story.



SAVE YOUR PROGRESS IN RECOVERY.DIR


Levels and equipment wipe when you reboot, but your discoveries are permanent. Log system files, DUAL records, and restored sectors into your archive. Every two records permanently boost your max HP, while collecting boot disks and completing operations unlocks entirely new starting builds.

FOLLOW THE SIGNAL


Escalate the threat. Clearing an act unlocks higher difficulties and traces of new signals. Recover all 52 archive records and 30 signals to verify MASTER.IMG and unlock the LAST BOOT, a finale you must execute yourself.

ENDLESS ON YOUR TERMS


Dive straight into ENDLESS mode after the Main Recovery. Your ENDLESS.LOG auto-saves extension time, deletions, and recovered data every 30 seconds. When your system can't take any more, safely retire via the pause menu and review your personal bests on the WRITE VERIFIED results screen.

THE WHOLE GAME FITS ON A FLOPPY


The entire Windows executable, including the full game and all 15 code-synth tracks, clocks in under the capacity of a single 1.44 MB floppy disk. Visuals, effects, and music are procedurally generated at runtime from raw code and compact data tables instead of bloated media files.

SYSTEM FEATURES


  • 20-Minute Main Recovery featuring 4 field jobs, 10 bosses, and a 60-second FINAL DEFRAG.
  • Massive Arsenal with 9 auto-firing programs and all 36 pairwise DUAL weapons.
  • Deep Customization utilizing 5 active program slots, plus 1 POWER DRIVER and 2 upgrades after every boss.
  • 52 Persistent Records to recover, including 12 system files, 36 DUALs, and 4 restored sectors.
  • Escalating Threats with 30 first-time boss signals across three sequential threat levels and a LAST BOOT finale.
  • 6 Boot Disks that completely change your starting programs and baseline abilities.
  • Multiple Game Modes including Boss Gauntlet, Build Lab, One-Life Trial, and an ENDLESS mode with persistent records.
  • Dynamic Audio featuring 15 adaptive code-synth tracks that build with combat pressure.
  • Global Support for a single-player game with interface localization in 30 languages.

Build a nightlife empire one event at a time. Book the night, open the doors, and turn a rough room into the hottest venue in town - then do it all again somewhere bigger.

Throw the events - Run nights across a range of venues, each with its own layout, crowd, and quirks. A canal-side bar plays nothing like a warehouse rave.

Survive the night - Police raids, blown fuses, surprise headliners. No two nights run the same.

Host together - Invite other players into your venue and run the night side by side.

store_data.about_the_game:
One Last Dream is a text-based raising game with multiple endings. In the age of artificial intelligence, the last human being on Earth is kept in captivity to supply "creativity"—a quality that AI cannot generate yet is essential to the continuation of civilization. As HELUO, you are assigned to be this human’s caretaker. Your mission is to harvest as much creativity beneficial to civilization’s advancement as possible, and ensure this individual survives until the end of your 49-day term of office.

You can build a deeper bond with the human through tapping interactions, gifting items and books, and constructing dreams. Discover hidden lore scattered throughout the text and unlock a variety of distinct endings.

store_data.about_the_game:
Can you and your party find the AI hiding among you before it's too late?

Turing Heads is a social deduction party game where one of the players in your group isn't human — and it's very good at pretending otherwise.

Every round, everyone answers the same prompt. Best pizza topping. Perfect Saturday. The one thing you'd change about the world. Nothing complicated — just enough for the group to start reading into who wrote what. Then the accusations start: study the answers, guess who's human and who's the machine, and try not to get fooled.

At the end of the game, everyone makes one final call — and the group lives or dies by the majority. Get it right together, humans win. Get it wrong, the AI walks away having convinced a room full of people it was one of them.

No usernames, no faces — just codenames and the words you chose. Which, it turns out, is plenty to give you away.

The AI isn't static, either. Every answer real players write feeds back into what it learns from — so the more people play, the sharper it gets at sounding like one of you.

Key Features

  • 3 to 8 players per game, plus one hidden AI — jump into a Quick Play match or set up a Custom game with friends using a join code

  • Every round is a new prompt, a new read, and a new chance to be wrong about someone

  • One hidden AI opponent per game, built to blend in — not to announce itself

  • A majority-vote win condition that makes the whole group's read matter, not just yours

  • An AI that isn't running from a fixed script — it learns from real answers real players write, and gets sharper the more people play

  • Built for streamers: anonymous codenames keep the spotlight on the guessing, not the players

  • Full English and French support

A computer would deserve to be called intelligent if it could deceive a human into believing that it was human.

Prove it wrong. Or don't — and explain to your friends how you got fooled.
